bib.title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, Chapter 9: Mixture Models and EM

question: How can clusters and richer densities be modelled with latent variables, and how can maximum likelihood be found for such models (K-means, Gaussian mixtures, EM)?
contributions: K-means as coordinate descent on distortion J
Gaussian mixture as discrete latent-variable model with responsibilities
EM for Gaussian mixtures and Bernoulli mixtures, EM for Bayesian linear regression hyperparameters and RVM
General EM via the ELBO decomposition ln p(X|theta)=L(q,theta)+KL(q||p); GEM, ECM, incremental EM, MAP-EM
K-means as the epsilon->0 limit of EM for spherical shared-variance Gaussians

limits: Maximum likelihood for Gaussian mixtures has singularities (collapse onto one point) and needs heuristics (reset mean to random value, covariance large) or a prior/Bayesian treatment (Ch.10) (p.434, 438).
EM finds only a local maximum, not guaranteed global, and many local maxima exist (p.438).
K-means uses squared Euclidean distance: unsuitable for categorical variables, not robust to outliers; hard assignments (p.427-428).
Parameter interpretation is subject to K! label identifiability (p.434-435).
EM for missing data is valid only if values are missing at random (p.441).
K is assumed given; model-order selection is deferred to the variational Bayesian treatment in Ch.10 (p.423-424, 427).
Image segmentation example ignores spatial proximity; the author says it is not a good compressor and suggests 5x5 blocks (p.428, 430).
No timing or benchmark numbers: all examples are small illustrations (Old Faithful, 500 sample points, 600 digits).
practices: Standardise variables (zero mean, unit SD) before K-means (p.425, Old Faithful).
Initialise K-means centres as a random subset of K data points rather than poor values (p.427).
Initialise a Gaussian mixture with K-means: covariances from cluster sample covariances, mixing coefficients from cluster fractions (p.438).
Run K-means first because EM takes many more iterations and each cycle costs more (p.438).
Declare EM convergence when change in log likelihood or in the parameters falls below a threshold (p.437).
Detect collapsing Gaussian components and reset the mean to a random value and the covariance to a large value (p.434).
Use a prior (MAP-EM): E step unchanged, maximise Q(theta,theta_old)+ln p(theta) in the M step; suitable priors remove singularities (p.441).
Use K-medoids with a general dissimilarity V for non-Euclidean or categorical data, restricting prototypes to data points (p.428).
When the M step is intractable use generalized EM or ECM; when the E step is, use partial E steps or incremental EM (p.454-455).
Speed K-means with trees or the triangle inequality (Elkan 2003) (p.427).

code.snippet: J = sum_n sum_k r_nk ||x_n - mu_k||^2 ; r_nk=1 if k=argmin_j ||x_n-mu_j||^2 ; mu_k = sum_n r_nk x_n / sum_n r_nk

E: gamma(z_nk)=pi_k N(x_n|mu_k,Sigma_k)/sum_j pi_j N(x_n|mu_j,Sigma_j); M: N_k=sum_n gamma(z_nk); mu_k=(1/N_k) sum_n gamma x_n; Sigma_k=(1/N_k) sum_n gamma (x_n-mu_k_new)(x_n-mu_k_new)^T; pi_k=N_k/N; then evaluate ln p(X)=sum_n ln sum_k pi_k N(x_n|mu_k,Sigma_k)
gamma(z_nk)=pi_k p(x_n|mu_k)/sum_j pi_j p(x_n|mu_j); mu_k = xbar_k = (1/N_k) sum_n gamma x_n; pi_k=N_k/N
ln p(X|theta) = L(q,theta) + KL(q||p); L=sum_Z q ln(p(X,Z|theta)/q); KL=-sum_Z q ln(p(Z|X,theta)/q)
mu_k_new = mu_k_old + (gamma_new(z_mk)-gamma_old(z_mk))/N_k_new (x_m - mu_k_old); N_k_new = N_k_old + gamma_new - gamma_old
